name: CR-Int-15-partialfrac-2.a
questiontext:
By expressing the integrand as the sum of its partial fractions, find the following definite integral:
\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
In order to calculate \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] we need to express the integrand as the sum of its partial fractions.

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 {{CT:2}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:4}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}}{{CT:6}} + {{CT:7}}{{CT:8}}
 \end{array}\]

By multiplying both sides by {{CT:9}} we get

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 {{CT:10}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}}+{{CT:12}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:13}}
 \end{array}\]

Equating coefficients we get a system of equations that can be solved to get \(A = {{CT:14}}\) and \(B = {{CT:15}}\).

So, \[{{CT:2}} = {{CT:16}}\]

Hence,
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:16}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:14}} \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}} + {{CT:15}} \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:17}} + {{CT:18}} +c
 \end{array}\]

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
  \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:19}} - [{{CT:20}}] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:21}}.
 \end{array}\]
